However, the conditions required by BCO 33-4 were not met. There is no indication that it was "impracticable immediately to commence process" against Mrs. Smith. In fact, process was commenced within a reasonable time.

artifacts.synopsis: Beverly R. Smith appealed her conviction on four charges (factiousness, gossip/slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy) by the session of Covenant Presbyterian Church, which was upheld by Southwest Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, finding the documentary evidence insufficient to prove the charges and that the session committed multiple procedural errors including failure to produce witnesses, prejudice, and improper suspension from the sacraments before charges were disclosed.

artifacts.title: Suspensions during pending process or delay under BCO 31-10
artifacts.disposition: not in conflict; Adopted by the CCB

matches.evidence: CCB found no constitutional conflict in proposed amendments to BCO 31-10 and 33-4 governing suspensions during judicial process or delay.

artifacts.title: Pre-trial non-disciplinary suspensions in judicial proceedings
